solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soldiers join forces? Well I never!

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
to ally is to join forces with another party

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about troops merging, followed by an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or disbelief, spoken when hearing startling news.

clue.text: City publisher embraced by left- winger recovered

indicators.note: something embraced is held in the arms of the other piece, so these letters sit inside

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist, someone on the political left
EC is the postcode area of the City of London
OUP is Oxford University Press

explanation.surface: A City publishing house has been taken over by a socialist, who got something back.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcode begins EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup losses is to win back money spent, so recovered is a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Story of English record conveyed in a message

indicators.note: carried inside something, so these letters are placed within the message

parts.note: a note is a short written message
a CD is a compact disc, a recording

explanation.surface: A tale about an English recording, passed on in a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short personal tale, a kind of story told in conversation.

clue.text: Instant good feeling that florist gives out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A florist hands out flowers that create a sudden warm emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes all three words 'that florist gives', including 'gives', which the surface treats as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names immediate romantic attraction on first meeting, an instant warm emotion.

clue.text: Quietly the female sits in building as farm-worker

indicators.note: one piece sitting in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a shed is a simple outbuilding
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
her is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman sits quietly inside an outbuilding while working on the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A shepherd tends sheep, one of the classic jobs of a farm labourer.

clue.text: Parties have hilarious person meeting English nurses with children

parts.note: someone very funny is called a hoot
nannies are nurses who look after children

explanation.surface: A funny guest at parties chats with an Englishman and childminders.
explanation.definitionFit: Hootenannies are informal gatherings with folk music and dancing, a lively kind of party.

clue.text: One on coach in old street occupying passenger seat

indicators.note: to occupy a seat is to be inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: a pillion is the passenger seat behind a motorcycle rider

explanation.surface: Someone in an old street sits in the passenger seat of a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' means a horse-drawn carriage, not a sports trainer or bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A postillion rides the leading horse drawing a carriage, so is a rider on a horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: Admiration satisfies head of empire turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to meet a demand is to satisfy it

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Admiration pleases the emperor as he appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard or respect for someone, closely equivalent to admiration.

clue.text: Put down some medicine, record for swallowing

indicators.note: something swallowed is taken inside, so these letters go within

parts.note: a dose is a measured quantity of medicine
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Instructions to set down some medicine and then a record for taking it.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a ruler is to remove them from power, which is to put them down.

clue.text: Split stick

definitions.meaning: to split wood is to chop it apart
to stick close is to cling to someone faithfully

explanation.walkthrough: The word is its own opposite: it means both to divide and to adhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleave has two contrary meanings, to cut apart and to cling to, matching each definition.

clue.text: Employment in sweaty work where roofer operates

indicators.note: one piece in another is placed inside it

parts.note: hot weather makes you sweaty
use is employment of something
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A job involving sweaty labour, the kind a roofer does up high.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofer works on the top of a building, which is a housetop.

clue.text: See 3
Language of some loud rumours going round

indicators.note: going round means the letters are turned back to front
some of means only part of the words is taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A tongue in which rumours are spread noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks UDRU from 'loud rumours' and 'going round' turns it back.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is a language spoken in Pakistan and India, the national tongue of Pakistan.

clue.text: Being stern and silent seems wrong, putting maiden off

indicators.note: seems wrong signals the letters are put into the wrong order

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Staying quiet when being severe appears mistaken, which puts a young woman off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting maiden off' removes M from the letters of 'silent seems'; the rest are rearranged ('wrong').
explanation.definitionFit: Steeliness is hard, unyielding resolve, the quality of being stern and inflexible.

clue.text: After-effect of drink knocking out good Scot in a royal house

indicators.note: knocking something out removes it from the word

parts.note: a hangover follows heavy drinking
Ian is a typical Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A hangover floors a Scotsman who lives in a palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Hanover ruled Britain from George I to Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hanoverian is a member of the British royal dynasty of Hanover, someone in that royal family line.

clue.text: Additional piece of furniture woman's brought in that could be sent abroad

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside the other letters

parts.note: extra means additional
a table is a piece of furniture
Di is a woman's name; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A woman brings in an extra table that could be shipped overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone extraditable can legally be handed over to another country for trial, that is sent abroad.

clue.text: This odd fellow engaging one in old Corinth

indicators.note: odd means peculiar, so the letters are rearranged
engaging means taking in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a man is a fellow
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A strange fellow who meets someone in ancient Corinth.
explanation.walkthrough: Corinth lay on an isthmus; the Isthmian Games were held there.
explanation.definitionFit: Isthmian describes the narrow neck of land at Corinth in Greece and its ancient games.

clue.text: Extra money made from hobby?

definitions.meaning: money paid on a loan or savings on top of the sum
a pastime or pursuit enjoyed for its own sake

explanation.surface: Can a pastime earn you extra cash?
explanation.definitionFit: Interest is both money earned on capital and a pastime one pursues.

clue.text: Modified language of man who can't choose work, young fellow

parts.note: Hobson's choice, from a stable owner, is no choice at all
a job is a piece of work
a son is a young male

explanation.surface: A language change by an undecided man, a job and a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hobson hired out horses, offering only the one nearest the door: 'Hobson's choice' means no real choice.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names Anglo-Indian words altered by adoption into English, a modified form of speech.

clue.text: Prickly part of garden below refreshment area

indicators.note: in a down entry, below means the garden piece comes after the refreshment area

parts.note: a bar serves drinks
a bed is a plot of soil for flowers

explanation.surface: A thorny flower bed sits beneath the drinks area in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbed means having sharp points or hooks, like barbed wire, and so prickly.

clue.text: Silly people do and it is ridiculous

indicators.note: the absurd arrangement signals the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A remark that foolish folk act and behave absurdly.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiots are foolish people, so the plural noun matches silly people.

clue.text: We will receive messages, what could be sadder notices

indicators.note: what the word could be is a rearrangement of its letters

parts.note: to notice something is to see it

explanation.surface: Recipients of unhappy letters speak of what might be sadder notices.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person plural, as if the answer itself were talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Addressees are the people to whom letters or messages are sent, so they receive them.

clue.text: That's exciting early invention left abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means dropped, so the letter is removed

parts.note: the wheel is one of humanity's earliest inventions

explanation.surface: Delight at a prehistoric discovery that was later discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Whee is an exclamation of delight or thrill, used when something is exciting.

clue.text: Jack meets a French girl when Wimbledon starts

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards
une is the French for a, in its feminine form used for a girl

explanation.surface: A man called Jack meets a French girl at the start of the tennis championships.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon, the London tennis championships, begins in late June.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wimbledon tennis tournament traditionally begins in the last weeks of that summer month.

clue.text: Shout abuse at rulers? There will be reservations

parts.note: to boo someone is to jeer at them
kings are rulers

explanation.surface: Jeering at monarchs would provoke misgivings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reservations' suggests doubts, but it means advance orders for seats or rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookings are reservations made in advance for tables, seats or rooms.

clue.text: Retreating American to waste away with worry, offering no resistance

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: US means American
to pine is to waste away through grief or longing

explanation.surface: A withdrawing American frets himself into a passive state.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means passive and spineless, failing to resist, as well as lying face upwards.

clue.text: Dissension of star, the thing evident in self-help enterprise

indicators.note: being evident in something means appearing within it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: DIY is do-it-yourself, home improvement done without hiring help
the sun is a star
it is the pronoun for a thing

explanation.surface: Disagreement among celebrities is apparent in a home improvement venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Disunity is lack of agreement or cohesion within a group, which is dissension.

clue.text: Gym enthusiast eats a bit of food

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym lessons
a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A fitness fanatic snacks on a morsel.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is a small edible nut, a typical little snack of food.
